forecasts.reason: Theory: the top-8 directions act on early/middle-layer features that pretraining laid down and Think-SFT keeps, so at 1.5x they do on Think-SFT (209 per sample, ~90 cap hits) about what they do on the base (1.5x roughly equals full RL), landing near M(1)=220.
The same early/middle-layer features get overdriven at 3x; on the base, 3x falls from 203 to 117, so Think-SFT should also drop below its 209, by less given its higher start; wide interval.

Theory: random directions do not sit on the features math text drives (8-11x less drive), so a random rank-8 edit at 3x leaves Think-SFT at its 209 baseline (random edits on the base are flat at 158-167; the noise control on Think-SFT gave 209).

Math and Code top-8 directions overlap on shared early-layer input features, so adding both at 1.5x acts like a Math dose near 2x, which overshoots (190 on the base at 2x) rather than reaching 1.5x's ~200.
Math at 1x (192) plus partly overlapping Code directions (Code alone 178) sums to an effective dose between 1x and 1.5x on the shared features, so between 192 and 200.
Random directions add nothing because they are off the features math text drives, so the control scores about the same as the Math top-8 edit alone (1.5x, mean of 4 samples 200).

With the cue prefilled, the top-8 directions add only through the early/middle-layer features; at 2x they overshoot (on hard328, 190 vs 203 at 1.5x), but the short MATH-500 problems lose less, so a little below the 1.5x edit's 456.
